h1: The 5 Best Echo Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Echo Leaf Blowers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five Echo leaf blowers compared on airflow, backpack versus handheld carry and gas versus cordless power across yard sizes.
summary: The Echo X Series 1110 CFM backpack is the most powerful model in the range we reviewed. The PB-770T is the commercial-grade backpack, the eFORCE 56V is the cordless handheld, the X Series 456 CFM handheld is the gas lightweight, and the PB-2520 is the entry handheld.
intro: Echo's lineup spreads across backpacks, gas handhelds and a cordless battery model, and the model names do little to tell them apart. The real differences are airflow, carry style and power source, and choosing the wrong combination for your yard means either wasted money or an exhausted arm.
We reviewed the Echo models in the data on paper, comparing CFM, carry style and power, and ranked the five that make sense to buy. Prices appear as buckets because they move often.

products.name: Echo 220 MPH 1110 CFM 79.9 cc Gas 2-Stroke X Series Backpack Blower
products.verdict: The flagship: 1110 CFM and 220 MPH from a 79.9 cc engine.
products.description:
The X Series backpack is a gas 2-stroke blower with a 79.9 cc engine, rated at 1110 CFM and 220 MPH. It sits in the $500+ bucket.

As the top airflow figure in the Echo lineup, it ranks above the PB-770T by about 350 CFM. The tradeoff is the highest price bucket and the weight and noise that come with a large engine.

It suits owners of acre-plus lots or anyone clearing wet leaves. The caveat is that smaller yards simply do not need this much output.
products.idealFor: Acre-plus lots and heavy wet leaves.

products.name: PB-770T - Echo Backpack Blower - Commercial Grade 63.3 cc
products.description:
The PB-770T is sold as a commercial-grade backpack blower with a 63.3 cc engine and 756 CFM. It also sits in the $500+ bucket.

It ranks second since it has less airflow than the X Series while costing in the same bucket. In its favor, the smaller engine usually means less bulk on your back.

It suits landscapers and large-property owners who want a backpack for long days. The caveat is that the 1110 CFM model gives more output for similar money.
products.idealFor: Large properties and long working days.
products.skipIf: You want maximum output per dollar.

products.name: Echo eFORCE 56V 151 MPH 526 CFM Cordless Battery Powered Handheld
products.verdict: A 56V battery handheld with 526 CFM and no fuel.
products.description:
The eFORCE is a cordless handheld running on a 56V battery, rated at 151 MPH and 526 CFM. It is in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks third because 526 CFM beats the gas handheld here, and a battery removes fuel mixing. The tradeoff against the backpacks is carry fatigue and runtime.

It suits a mid-sized suburban yard. The caveat is that the data lists no runtime, so check battery details.
products.idealFor: Mid-sized yards where quiet and no fuel matter.
products.skipIf: You clear a very large property.

products.name: Echo 172 MPH 456 CFM 25.4 cc Gas 2-Stroke X Series Handheld Leaf
products.verdict: A gas handheld with 456 CFM and 172 MPH.
products.description:
This X Series handheld has a 25.4 cc 2-stroke gas engine rated at 456 CFM and 172 MPH. It sits in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks fourth because the cordless eFORCE has more airflow at the same bucket, though gas offers unlimited runtime if you refuel. The 172 MPH air speed helps move stuck debris.

It suits owners who prefer gas power in a light handheld. The caveat is two-stroke fuel mixing.
products.idealFor: Owners wanting a gas handheld for medium yards.
products.skipIf: You want to avoid fuel mixing.

products.name: echosari ECHO PB-2520 25.4cc Handheld Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The least expensive Echo handheld, though specs are thin.
products.description:
The PB-2520 is a 25.4 cc handheld blower in the $100-200 bucket, the lowest price here. The data gives no airflow figure.

It ranks last because without a stated CFM we cannot compare it to the others on output, and its listing title is oddly worded. The cost is the draw.

It suits small yards and light cleanup. The caveat is the missing airflow number, so check it first.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed CFM number.

whatMatters.detail: CFM is the volume of air and MPH is its speed. CFM clears bulk while MPH dislodges stuck debris. Look for both numbers in the listing title.
A backpack spreads weight across your back. A handheld is lighter to grab but tiring over time. Check the carry style in the specs.
Gas gives long runtime but needs fuel mixing, while a battery is quiet but finite. Check whether the title says 2-stroke or 56V.
Displacement in cc hints at power. A 79.9 cc engine is far bigger than a 25.4 cc one. Match it to the CFM figure.
A listing missing CFM is hard to judge. Verify the figure on the manufacturer page before you buy.

faq.a: The X Series backpack at 1110 CFM and 220 MPH tops the range we reviewed.

faq.q: Do Echo gas blowers need mixed fuel?
faq.a: The X Series models are 2-stroke, which typically means mixed fuel. Check the manual for the ratio.

faq.q: Is the eFORCE worth it over a gas handheld?
faq.a: Its 526 CFM beats the 456 CFM gas handheld and skips fuel. Check battery runtime for your yard.

faq.q: Why is the PB-2520 ranked last?
faq.a: The data gives no airflow figure, so we cannot compare its output. Verify CFM before buying.

faq.q: Can a handheld clear a large yard?
faq.a: The eFORCE and X Series handheld can for medium yards, but a backpack saves fatigue.

faq.q: How do I maintain a gas blower?
faq.a: Use fresh fuel and keep the air filter clean. Drain fuel before long storage.

finalTake: For most Echo buyers with a big property, the X Series 1110 CFM backpack is the top choice. The PB-770T suits commercial use, the eFORCE is best for quiet cordless work, and the smaller handhelds fit light cleanup.
